articles.title: Noisy Text in RAG: Typos, OCR, and the Gap Classical Spell-Check Leaves
articles.reason: Addresses a practical RAG challenge—handling noisy enterprise text (typos, OCR errors)—directly relevant to building robust retrieval systems for finance and insurance clients.
articles.summary: The article analyzes how noisy text from user input, transcription, and OCR impacts retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, highlighting the limitations of classical spell-checkers and the role of embeddings. It discusses real-world document intelligence scenarios where these issues degrade retrieval accuracy, which is critical for enterprise use cases. The piece suggests mitigation strategies that can be applied to improve RAG reliability in production environments.
actionable_insights: Audit current RAG pipelines for vulnerability to noisy text, especially OCR and transcription errors.

articles.title: Foundry Model Router Expands from Two Regions to 28, Refreshing Its Model Pool
articles.reason: This update directly impacts Azure OpenAI deployments, offering broader regional availability and new model options relevant for enterprise GenAI workflows.
articles.summary: Microsoft's Foundry model router now supports 28 regions, significantly expanding deployment flexibility for global and EU-based clients. The addition of Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 to the model pool enables access to the latest LLM capabilities, while automatic pool updates streamline maintenance. Consultants should note that the context window is limited by the smallest model in the pool, which may affect multi-model orchestration.
actionable_insights: Review and update model pool configurations to leverage new Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 capabilities in enterprise workflows.
Assess regional deployment options for compliance with EU data residency requirements, especially for finance and insurance clients.
Check and adjust agentic pipeline designs to account for context window limitations when using mixed model pools.
